Definition: Rameses or Raamses, a place in Egypt
BiblicalUsage: Rameses was a place in Egypt — a treasure city Pharaoh made Israel build. Joseph settled his father and brothers in the best of the land there, and it was the starting point of the exodus, when Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth.
TheologicalSignificance: What this says to me is that Rameses holds both ends of the story: the slavery Israel built with her hands, and the night she walked out of it.
